title: Choosing Wisely Canada climate-conscious recommendations for critical care medicine
one_line_summary: Seven evidence-based Choosing Wisely Canada recommendations providing pragmatic guidance for **critical** care clinicians to safely reduce the environmental footprint and supply waste of intensive care unit care.
key_pearls: - Daily provision of **critical** care generates **88–178 kg of CO2-equivalents** and **1.1–13.7 kg of material waste** per patient.
- Disposable gloves carry the highest carbon and water footprint among single-use ICU items; routine glove use when hand hygiene is sufficient should be avoided.
- Routine changes of ventilator circuits or in-line suction catheters do not improve outcomes and may increase the risk of **ventilator-associated pneumonia**.

- Transitioning from IV to oral/enteral drug administration reduces greenhouse emissions **significantly**, with IV antibiotics generating **10–70 times higher CO2-equivalents** than enteral equivalents.
- Medication reconciliation prior to ICU discharge should explicitly target deprescribing ICU-specific therapies that are no longer indicated.
- Keeping surplus supply stock outside patient rooms prevents unnecessary disposal of clean items upon patient discharge or transfer.
consensus_method: Three-stage structured anonymous voting process following scoping literature review and multidisciplinary consensus meetings

recommendation_blocks.narrative:
- Gloves are indicated only when contact with bodily fluids or visibly soiled items is anticipated.
- In ICU settings, disposable gloves account for **108 gloves per patient day**, representing the largest single-use carbon and water footprint hotspot.
- Inappropriate glove use for low-risk procedures ranges from **16.7% to 92%** and leads to reduced hand hygiene adherence and increased cross-contamination.

recommendations.statement: Do not use gloves when hand hygiene is sufficient.

recommendation_blocks.topic: Ventilator Circuit and In-Line Suction Maintenance
recommendation_blocks.narrative:
- Scheduled routine changes of ventilator tubing or in-line suction catheters offer no clinical benefit in adult or pediatric populations.
- Frequent circuit changes have been associated with an increased incidence of **ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)**.
- Circuit and catheter replacement should occur only when equipment is visibly soiled or malfunctioning.

recommendations.statement: Do not change ventilator tubing or in-line suction catheters unless they are visibly soiled.

recommendation_blocks.narrative:
- Unused single-use supplies kept inside patient rooms are frequently discarded upon transfer or discharge due to infection control protocols.
- Discarding clean unused items creates substantial material waste and financial loss.
- Restructuring workflows by maintaining supply carts outside rooms and utilizing small on-demand baskets markedly decreases supply waste.

recommendations.statement: Do not bring surplus supplies or equipment into patient care rooms if they will require disposal after patient transfer/discharge.

recommendation_blocks.narrative:
- IV drug delivery generates **10–70 times higher** CO2-equivalents for antibiotics, **8–66 times higher** for analgesics, **2 times higher** for **levetiracetam**, and **60 times higher** for **phosphate** compared to enteral routes.
- IV therapy incurs additional waste from syringes, IV tubing, and fluid bags.
- Enteral formulations of drugs such as **lansoprazole**, **acetaminophen**, **levetiracetam**, and **phosphate** demonstrate clinical efficacy or noninferiority compared to IV forms.

recommendations.statement: Do not continue intravenous medications when an oral/enteral alternative is equally safe and effective.

recommendation_blocks.narrative:
- Reusable medical items generally demonstrate lower lifecycle carbon footprints than single-use alternatives.
- Validated reusable options in **critical** care include **laryngoscopes**, **blood pressure cuffs**, **pulse oximeters**, **isolation gowns**, and **procedural instruments**.
- Evidence does not demonstrate **superior** infection prevention with single-use devices over appropriately decontaminated reusable equipment.

recommendations.statement: Do not use single-use/disposable items when a reusable option is available and less resource-intensive.

recommendation_blocks.narrative:
- Patients under isolation precautions generate **significantly** higher volume of gown, glove, and single-use waste.
- Isolation gowns and nonsterile gloves are key ICU **environmental hotspots** for greenhouse emissions and water consumption.
- Empowering clinical staff to promptly discontinue unnecessary isolation precautions according to **Infection Prevention and Control (IPAC)** guidance safely reduces waste.

recommendations.statement: Do not continue patient isolation precautions (e.g., shield, gown, gloves) after it is safe to discontinue such precautions in accordance with infection prevention and control practices.

recommendation_blocks.narrative:
- Pharmaceuticals comprise nearly **25%** of overall healthcare emissions in developed nations.
- ICU discharge transitions are prone to medication errors and inappropriate continuation of short-term ICU drugs.
- Standardized checklists, pharmacist-led reconciliation, and clinician education effectively facilitate deprescribing at ICU transfer.

recommendations.statement: Do not transfer a patient out of the intensive care unit without completing a medication reconciliation process and deprescribing intensive care unit-specific medications that are no longer indicated.

strengths_limitations:
- Strengths: National multidisciplinary panel representing physicians, nurses, respiratory therapists, pharmacists, dietitians, and trainees; rigorous three-round consensus methodology informed by scoping literature reviews.
- Limitations: Focuses exclusively on clinician-level decisions rather than hospital infrastructure, energy sourcing, or procurement; lacks patient/family and engineering representation; recommendations tailored to high-income country ICUs with potential regional variance in energy grids.

drugs_doses.indication: Gastric acid suppression / stress ulcer prophylaxis in critically ill patients
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: IV administration generates higher environmental footprint; enteral disintegrating tablet provides effective acid suppression

drugs_doses.indication: Seizure prophylaxis and treatment in critical care
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: IV route produces 2-fold higher CO2-equivalent emissions compared to oral/enteral administration

drugs_doses.indication: Mild-to-moderate hypophosphatemia in critically ill patients
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: IV phosphate replacement generates 60-fold higher CO2-equivalents compared to enteral replacement

drugs_doses.indication: Analgesia and antipyresis in ICU patients
drugs_doses.adverse_effects: IV administration carries 8–66 times higher environmental footprint than enteral route
